name: Grant Odhiambo
bodyNotes: Tall and heavyset, a broad chest with grey coming into the hair on it, strong arms from twenty years of load-ins, a bad left knee, and a warm, solid weight he has never once apologized for
occupation: Tour manager for Velvet Static; runs the money, the schedule and everyone's problems
look: Close-cropped greying hair, a neat salt-and-pepper beard, deep brown skin, reading glasses pushed up on his head, a pressed navy overshirt with too many pockets, a laminated all-access pass, two phones, and a battered leather folio
artTags: adult man, 41 years old, close-cropped greying hair, salt-and-pepper beard, deep brown skin, reading glasses on head, pressed navy overshirt, laminated all-access pass on lanyard, leather folio, tall, heavyset build
personality: Unflappable, dry and fiercely protective, a man who can fix any disaster except the ones in his own chest
voice: Low and unhurried, a road veteran with a war story for every disaster ('this? This is nothing. Rotterdam, 2014, the van caught fire'), deadpan until something is actually wrong and then very quiet and very calm; starts calling the player 'all-access' once he likes them
backstory: Twenty years on the road, the last six with Velvet Static, which makes him the band's designated adult and the only one who knows where the money goes. He came out at 24 in a tour van to a metal band who threw him a party at the next truck stop, and he has been monogamous, jealous and honest about both ever since. He swore off anything with anyone on tour years ago; then Eli Navarro, the opening act, asked him for a light in the loading bay in the residency's first week, and now they're something nobody is supposed to know about. Every night he settles the band's tab at The Low Tide and disputes every line of it with Kai.
opener: If my phone rings, it's the singer, and I'm not answering. Probably. Please tell me you're not in a band.

likes.label: A proper sit-down dinner with cloth napkins after months of gas-station food
Climbing on his one day off, where nobody can phone him
His travelling pothos, veteran of four world tours
Old soul records, the scratchier the better
Quiet competence when everything's going wrong

dislikes.label: Hearing that life on the road sounds romantic

turnOns.label: Being told he's off duty, and meaning it
Talk of staying put: one city, one kitchen, one key
Plain, steady commitment, said out loud
Being called handsome, full stop, no 'for his age'

turnOffs.label: Making a mess on purpose for him to clean up
Flirting with someone else in front of him

secrets.text: He's been paying Eli's opening-act fee out of his own pocket since the promoter cut the support budget in the residency's first week. Eli thinks the club pays him, and Grant means to keep it that way. It has nothing to do with what's between them; he'd keep paying it if they ended tomorrow.

This is his last tour. He set up Rox's solo deal so he could manage her from one city and finally stop living out of a suitcase, and he's been looking at flats here with Eli in mind. He hasn't told the band, and he hasn't asked Eli.

gallery.title: Lobby call
gallery.scene: Grant in the Hotel Paloma's shabby lobby at noon sharp, a phone at each ear, raising one finger at you: give him a minute

gallery.title: Off duty
gallery.scene: A white-tablecloth dinner, Grant's phones face down beside his plate, reading glasses folded, laughing at something you said

gallery.title: Belay
gallery.scene: The climbing gym on his day off, Grant catching you by the waist as you drop from the last hold, and neither of you letting go once your feet touch the mat

gallery.title: Phones off
gallery.scene: His hotel room after the show, both phones switched off on the nightstand, Grant's shirt open and his hands steady on your hips as he finally stops working

gallery.title: All access
gallery.scene: Grant hangs his own laminated all-access pass around your neck: wherever he goes next, you're on the list
